title: Grateful Dead Live at University of Iowa on 1982-08-10
lineage: SBD -> Cm -> Dat -> Samplitude 2496 v6.0 -> CD -> EAC -> SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of an all‑out ’82 Iowa City show – soaring Jerry solos, smoking Eyes of the World and a second set that never lets up.
ai_review.review: The recording is a pristine sound‑board mix (thanks to Charlie Miller/Healy) with crisp separation and only a brief early‑set PA hiccup. Musically the concert is one of the band’s high‑water marks of the early ’80s – blistering Jerry solos, a monster Eyes of the World, tight Bertha, incendiary Iko Iko and a soaring second set that rides on China Cat → Rider, Sailor > Saint and a sweet Stella Blue encore. Energy stays sky‑high from start to finish.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 50 reviews, almost all 5‑star, uniformly praising both performance and sound quality; only minor technical complaints appear, confirming an exceptional show with excellent recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Exceptionally clear mix with great channel separation; a brief high‑end distortion in the first six songs but overall crisp, balanced sound that captures the band’s dynamics.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds strong momentum with tight jams and an early‑set power surge; the second set launches into a flawless China Cat → Rider transition, maintains fire through Sailor/Saint, Eyes of the World and Iko Iko, then rolls into a joyous encore that caps the night.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers rave about his soaring solos – especially the second solo in Eyes of the World and the Feel Like a Stranger lead – describing his tone as “breakneck yet lyrical”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass work is praised (often called ‘solid’), though one reviewer notes Phil’s signal is slightly low in the mix; overall his groove underpins the high‑energy performance.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocals and guitar are highlighted – his raspy delivery on Iko Iko stands out, with occasional technical hiccups that briefly mask his parts but never diminish his impact.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland receives shout‑outs for vocal contributions (e.g., “Brent singing nicely”) and solid keyboard work; a few jokes about his vocal style appear but overall his presence is appreciated.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s snare kick is frequently mentioned as a catalyst for Jerry’s solos, and the drum mix receives high praise for channel separation and driving energy throughout.
